name: New Zealand
prevalence_note: New Zealand 2025-2026 warnings: bank Fraud and Security Team Impersonation Scam; remote Access IT and Telecommunications Support Scam; government Tax and Official Agency Impersonation Scam; impersonated Family Emergency Money Scam.
cross_border_note: Many of these calls come from overseas call centres in English.

scams.name: Bank Fraud Team Impersonation Scam
scams.name_en: Bank Fraud and Security Team Impersonation Scam
scams.signals_en: Callers spoof official bank numbers and claim to be from the bank's fraud or security team investigating an unauthorized overseas payment.
scams.legit_en: Real banks in Australia and New Zealand never ask customers to share passwords, PINs, or one-time verification codes over the phone, and never tell customers to move money into a separate safe account.
bait_tactics: Oh gosh, that sounds worrying—my banking app is spinning on a loading screen right now, could you tell me which account type that payment came from?
Sorry, the mobile reception in the back room here is patchy—could you slowly repeat your reference number while I grab a notepad?
I never read codes out over the phone, so how about you pop a secure message inside my banking app inbox and I'll check it properly?

scams.name: Remote Access Tech and Broadband Scam
scams.name_en: Remote Access IT and Telecommunications Support Scam

red_flag_keywords.text: log into your online banking to check

scams.signals_en: Callers claim to represent a telecommunications provider, internet service team, or computer security department, warning that the recipient's broadband line or computer has been hacked.
scams.legit_en: Legitimate telecommunications carriers and software providers in Australia and New Zealand never make unsolicited phone calls asking users to install remote-access tools, and never ask customers to open online banking during troubleshooting.
bait_tactics: Hang on, my laptop takes ages to boot up after an update—which error message did you say my modem was sending through?
I'm only on a mobile handset right now and don't have a computer in front of me, can you post out a letter explaining the line fault?
The wireless network in this part of the house keeps dropping out, could you walk me through what the issue is without installing anything?

scams.name: Government Tax and Anti-Scam Agency Impersonation
scams.name_en: Government Tax and Official Agency Impersonation Scam
scams.signals_en: Scammers pretend to be tax officers, police, or national anti-scam investigators, claiming an overdue tax debt or alleging the victim's mobile number was linked to overseas fraud.
scams.legit_en: Government revenue offices and anti-scam agencies in Australia and New Zealand never threaten immediate arrest by phone, never ask for portal passwords, and never demand payment via gift cards or cryptocurrency.
bait_tactics: Right, our tax paperwork is filed away in the study—could you give me the correspondence reference so we can check our official online inbox?
That sounds like a mix-up, could you repeat your department name slowly while I jot it down to verify through the main switchboard?
I can't open any links or portals while I'm on a voice call, so is an official notice already on its way in the post?

scams.name: Urgent Family or Friend New-Number Scam

red_flag_keywords.text: transfer money urgently to this account
pay this invoice for me right now

scams.signals_en: Callers pose as a close family member or friend calling from an unfamiliar number, claiming their phone was broken or lost and they are in an urgent bind or accident.
scams.legit_en: Real relatives with a broken phone can still confirm shared family details or wait while you ring their original number or check with another family member on a separate channel.
bait_tactics: Oh goodness, the line sounds really muffled—which cousin is this again, and what happened to your usual number?
I don't have banking set up on this handset, let me quickly ring your old phone or check with the rest of the family first.
Slow down a bit so I can catch what happened—whereabouts are you right now, and why is it a different bank account?
